mentions.snippet: Explicit buyer-warning thread on a diesel truck forum about King main thrust bearings. Title itself is a warning to other builders, which is the most damaging shape a mention can take.

mentions.title: King Main Bearings Defective
mentions.snippet: Reports that King STDX main bearings had thrust bearings over 1mm too narrow to fit multiple BMW blocks, across both S85 and S65 engines. A dimensional defect reproducing on more than one engine family.

mentions.title: King main and rod bearings marked STDX
mentions.snippet: Builder reports 2024 King thrust bearings out of spec on free spread, with a 2025 production run said to show the same problem. Repeat-batch manufacturing claim, not a one-off install error.
mentions.replyNote: Thread read successfully; no King or official brand representative has replied, and it remains open and unresolved.

mentions.title: King Bearing - lack of professional help for quality control problem
mentions.snippet: Customer received a sealed package with mismatched shell sizes (8 upper .011, 7 lower .011, 1 lower .030) and says King refused to send a replacement pair, redirecting him to the supplier. Packing defect plus a service complaint.

mentions.title: King Bearing Failures?
mentions.snippet: King main and rod bearings reported failing during initial startup and break-in with metal and debris in the oil filter, though other posters suggest another root cause for that build.

mentions.title: king Main&Rod Bearings?
mentions.snippet: Poster reports spinning King rod bearings twice in three months on a boosted setup. Credible repeat failure, though a boosted application leaves lubrication as a competing explanation.
